claims: Palm Sunday commemorates Jesus's triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
Palm Sunday marks the start of Holy Week.
Palm Sunday marks Jesus's final week before his crucifixion and resurrection.
Jesus approached Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives.
Jesus sent disciples to find a donkey colt.
Zechariah 9:9 prophesies that the King would come lowly and riding on a donkey.
A large crowd gathered to welcome Jesus.
The crowd had heard of Jesus's miracles, especially raising Lazarus.
The crowd spread palm branches on the road.
Palm branches are symbols of victory, peace, and triumph.
The crowd spread their own cloaks on the road to form a carpet.
The people shouted "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!".
"Hosanna" is a Hebrew phrase meaning "save us" or "save now".
Jesus rode a donkey instead of a horse or chariot.
The crowds cheered.
Religious leaders (Pharisees) questioned the praise.
Jesus told the Pharisees that if the people kept quiet, the rocks would cry out.
After entering the city, Jesus went to the Temple.
Jesus drove out the money changers who were exploiting worshippers.
Palm Sunday is celebrated on the Sunday before Easter.
Churches often distribute palm fronds during the service.
